transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Honestly, it’s mainly work. I keep getting up when I’m not supposed to. Like, I’ll be at my station and I’m supposed to stay there, obviously, because it’s a production floor and there are rules for a reason, but I’ll just… leave. Not like I’m trying to be difficult or sneak off, it’s more like my body is already moving before I’ve really thought it through.

And it happens in meetings too. If we’re supposed to sit there and listen, I’ll pop up or start moving around, and then afterward I’m like, why did I do that? My supervisor has talked to me about it more than once, and now she’s saying it’s becoming a safety problem because I’ll just take off from my station too fast or at the wrong time. That kind of scared me, because I don’t want to get hurt or get someone else hurt, and I don’t want to lose my job. So… yeah, that’s why I came in.
When you get up from your station or in meetings, do you feel a strong inner restlessness or urge to move right before it happens?

Yeah, definitely. It’s not just like I randomly decide, “I’m going to get up now.” It’s more like this feeling starts building in me, like pressure or buzzing almost, especially if I’m trying to stand still by the machine or sit through training. I’ll be telling myself, okay, stay put, don’t move, just wait, but my body feels like it’s getting tighter and tighter.

And then I feel like I have to do something right then — move my legs, stretch, pace, go check something, anything. If I try to ignore it, it gets really uncomfortable, like I can’t think about anything except needing to move. Then before I know it, I’m already walking away or shifting around. It feels more like an urge in my body than a choice I’m calmly making.
Right before you get up or move, do you have a repetitive unwanted thought that makes you feel like you have to do it?

I don’t think so. Not like a thought-thought, if that makes sense. I’m trying to think because I don’t want to answer it wrong, but I don’t notice some specific idea in my head like, “You have to get up or something bad will happen,” or anything repeating like that.

It’s more physical for me. Like my body feels uncomfortable and keyed up, and then I’m just focused on needing to move. Sometimes I might think, “I can’t sit here anymore,” but it doesn’t feel like an unwanted thought that’s making me do it. It’s more like the thought comes after the feeling, if that makes sense. The feeling is what pushes it.
Did you have the same kind of trouble staying seated or keeping still when you were a child?

Yeah. Yeah, I did. Honestly, that’s kind of been me as far back as I can remember, even in elementary school.

I was the kid who couldn’t just sit in the chair like everyone else. I’d be up out of my seat, wandering around the room, or turning around talking to somebody when the teacher was trying to teach. And I didn’t always mean to be rude, but I’d talk over the teacher or blurt things out before I was supposed to. Like if I knew an answer, or even if I just had something pop into my head, it would come out of my mouth before I really thought about raising my hand or waiting.

I remember getting notes sent home for that kind of stuff — talking too much, interrupting, not staying in my seat, moving around when I wasn’t supposed to. It wasn’t just once or twice. It was a thing teachers noticed about me. So yeah, the keeping still part has been there since I was little.
When someone in authority tells you what to do, do you often argue with them?

I don’t know if I’d say I argue with them a lot. Like, not just because they’re in charge or because I want to fight with them. I mean, I might ask questions if I don’t understand why they want something done a certain way, and sometimes maybe that comes off like I’m pushing back, but in my head I’m usually trying to understand it or I’m reacting in the moment.

So… I guess I’m not sure. I don’t think I’m constantly arguing with bosses or teachers just to be difficult. If anything, I might get a little defensive if I feel like someone’s coming at me wrong, but I wouldn’t say I’m always arguing with authority, no.
Do you often have trouble keeping your attention on a task, even when you want to focus?

Yeah, definitely. Even when I actually want to focus, it’s like my brain won’t stay locked onto it.

Like at work, when I’m doing inventory logs, I’ll start out really trying to do it right because I know the numbers matter. I’ll be looking at the sheet or the screen, and for the first minute or two I’m okay, but then after a little bit the numbers just kind of run together. I’ll realize I’ve been staring at the same line and I don’t actually know what I just counted or wrote down, so I have to go back and check it again.

Same thing with reading the CNC training pages. I’ll tell myself, “Okay, just read this section and pay attention,” but after a few minutes the words start blurring together, not literally like my vision, but like I’m seeing them and not taking them in. Then I get to the end of a paragraph and I’m like, wait, I have no idea what that said. So I have to reread the same part over and over, and it takes way longer than it should. It’s frustrating because it’s not that I don’t care. I’m trying, but it just doesn’t stick.
